text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

-The government's long-term plan will be discussed in parliament today. The opposition criticises Prime Minister Thorjoern Jagland for being unclear in policy and trying to spread resources over too many areas.

-Two of the four people who suffered food-poisoning at MacDonald's on Sunday will probably sue the fast-food company. Two employees and two customers were taken to hospital after eating MacDonald's MacLaks salmon burgers.

-The fishfarming industry will react strongly against producers who violate the salmon agreement with the European Union (EU). Norway and the EU reached an agreement on Sunday, which means Norway will avoid anti-dumping duties on salmon export.

-Ole Lund, head of the board of the Oslo stock exchange, says he sees a common Nordic bourse in a long-term perspective. Despite the Oslo bourse's decision to use a different trading system from that on the Swedish exchange, Lund sees no problems against cooperation.

-After several acquisitions Canadian Potash Corp of Saskatchewan is threathening the position of Norway's Norsk Hydro as the world largest fertiliser producer. Hydro, however, says the most important factor is to be profitable and not necessarily the largest producer.

-The United Nations (U.N.) owes the Norwegian state 400 million crowns for a number of missions by Norwegian forces. Since 1980 the U.N.'s debt to Norway has increased from 124 million crowns to more than 400 million.
